- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is trending down, adjust downward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overoptimism.  
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value by 5–15% to account for overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply upward bias correction by 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more), reduce forecast smoothness and add 2–5% lag correction to align with recent trend.  
- If sentiment is flat (±0.1) and forecast diverges from history, apply “stick to recent 7-day average” heuristic to avoid drift.
